subject: [Borealis] Commit sizing & surge sandwich — pilot capacity proposal
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Commit sizing & surge sandwich — pilot capacity proposal

Hi Sanjay / team,

Thanks for the numbers you shared in the discovery — really helpful. Attached is a short simulation (borealis-surge-sim.csv) and a draft of our pilot capacity proposal (redwood-proposal-draft-v2.pdf). High-level asks:

- Confirm target SLO: p95 <= 450ms for chat completions (user -> assistant end-to-end) and p50 <= 120ms for short prompt inference (<= 128 tokens).
- Confirm expected steady-state tokens/sec: you mentioned 1.8M tokens/day; sanity-checking as 21 tps average during business hours with 3x peak bursts.

We ran quick estimates against a 13B-ish encoder-decoder family (float16 baseline) and a 70B decoder variant (quantized) for fallbacks. Our initial recommendation:

- Dedicated cluster: start with 8x A100-80GB-equivalent slots (or 5x H100-equivalent if you prefer H100 SKU), allocated as two pool tiers:
  * Primary pool (6 GPUs): low-latency p95 SLO target for chat (short-medium length).
  * Burst reserve (2 GPUs): absorbs 3x short-duration spikes; warmed by KV caching warmup and prefix caching.

- Ops buffer: +25% headroom on top of modeled peak to account for cold starts, canary rollouts, and 10% traffic growth in first 90 days.

Notes and open items in the CSV: token distribution by endpoint, sequences per call, median/90/95 token lengths, and assumed batching windows.

Next steps: if you confirm SLO and commit size (monthly tokens or dedicated slot commitment), we’ll produce a final commitment worksheet and a proposed canary schedule.

Thanks — Jordan

Jordan — thanks for the quick turnaround and the simulation artifacts. A few clarifications from our side:

- SLO: p95 <= 400ms is our internal bar for chat (we prefer to push toward 400 if feasible). We can accept p50 <= 120ms for short prompts.
- Traffic profile: yes ~1.8M tokens/day is baseline; daytime window (09:00–18:00 PT) concentrates 70% of load; expected burst factor is closer to 4x during product launches.
- Budget: we are prioritizing predictability. Procurement asked for committed-slot pricing with a 12-month minimum and an explicit burst allowance.

Can you update the plan to target p95=400ms and include a 4x burst scenario plus clear canary steps? Also please include a short note on data handling (KV cache TTLs, keys stored, retention) — compliance team will read that.

-Sanjay

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 13:00:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Re: Commit sizing & surge sandwich — pilot capacity proposal

Ben / Kim — forwarding Sanjay's ask. Key changes they want: p95 -> 400ms, burst 4x, 12-mo committed slot with burst allowance, and a short compliance blurb on KV cache retention.

Below are my updated quick numbers — please review and correct:

Summary (targeting p95=400ms):
- Workload assumptions:
  * Model family: primary = 13B dec/enc-dec (float16), fallback = 70B quantized (int8/q4) for quality spikes
  * Mean tokens per call: 180 (chat flows); median 60; 95th 620
  * Peak concurrency: 320 concurrent requests during launch-day bursts

- Throughput math (conservative):
  * Measured single A100 perf (approx): 13B float16 -> 12.5 tokens/sec p95 under 400ms SLA on 1k-token windows (continuous); 70B int8 fallback -> 22 tokens/sec for generation-heavy workloads (note: larger models can have worse tail latency due to KV size)
  * Effective tps per GPU (realistic for mixed-length): assume 18 tps/GPU
  * Required GPUs at 4x burst (targeting no queueing at p95): ceil(peak_tps / 18). Peak_tps estimated: baseline peak 210 tps -> 4x = 840 tps -> 840/18 ≈ 47 GPUs -> This is obviously too large for a pilot.

- Practical dedicated pilot proposal (tradeoff):
  * Start: 8 GPUs dedicated (A100-equivalent). Expect sustained capacity about 8*18 = ~144 tps. With request shaping + short-fail fallbacks we can meet p95=400ms for 90% of traffic and absorb moderate peaks via burst pool + routing to fallback quantized variants.
  * Burst reserve: additional 4 ephemeral GPUs (pre-warmed H100s if available) in Dedicated but on standby via burst policy. These will be billed as committed burst allowance for the 12-mo term.
  * Traffic shaping plan: adaptive rate-limiting + circuit-breaker to route high-latency flows to the 70B quantized fallback (slower but higher token throughput) and a lightweight summarizer to reduce token-length per call.

- Headroom rationale: 25% on top of modeled peak for steady ops, plus explicit 4x launch-day runway managed by burst pool and weighted routing.

Open technical items for Ben: I used 18 tps/GPU as a coarse blended number. Please sanity-check with the kernel mix (attn-type, kv-cache hit rate) and advise recommended GPU SKUs (A100 vs H100) and whether we should propose mixed-sku pools.

Also add a one-paragraph compliance blurb: KV cache TTL default 24 hours, encrypted at rest with customer KMS; explicit retention gates for audit requests. That should satisfy their compliance team for a pilot.

If we cannot meet p95=400ms on 8+4 model, propose pricing that includes optional burst-invocation credits tied to documented launch windows.

Jordan
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@borealis.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 16:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Commit sizing & surge sandwich — pilot capacity proposal

Quick tech sanity checks / corrections:

- tps/GPU: 18 tps is conservative for mixed workloads; with strong batching and KV hit > 60% we can push to ~28 tps/GPU on A100 for the 13B family. H100 will be ~35 tps under similar conditions. The tail (p95) is dominated by KV cache misses and long-history contexts.

- Burst math: Jordan's peak_tps estimate (840 tps) looks correct for a naive 4x multiple of a 210 baseline but we should avoid sizing purely for extreme launch spikes. Instead:
  * Committed baseline: 12 GPUs (expect ~12*25 = 300–360 tps blended with caching)
  * Burst pool: 12 ephemeral GPUs that are pre-warmed during 2-hour windows around planned launches — this gives a practical 2x amplification without permanently overprovisioning.
  * If Borealis insists on 4x always-on headroom, pricing should reflect a higher commit (45–50 GPUs) or call out surge credits explicitly.

- Recommendation: propose a two-tier commercial option:
  1) Pilot commit (12 GPUs dedicated + 4 burst equiv, 12-mo) — reliable for day-to-day and modest launches, hit p95=400ms for ~95% traffic with routing rules.
  2) Launch protection add-on (pre-warmed 12 GPU window + surge credits) — for discrete launches (billed when invoked).

- Ops notes: KV cache TTL 24h default; enable predictive cache pre-warm for planned campaigns; set cold-start reserve of 10% GPUs to keep latency tails bounded during canary deploys.

I can prepare a short table of tps/GPU by model & kv-hit% and attach to the proposal.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is exactly the granularity we needed. Two quick decisions from our side:

1) We accept the Pilot commit option (12 GPUs + 4 burst equiv) with a documented launch protection add-on. Procurement will review terms and DocuSign the 12-mo commitment this week.
2) Compliance: the KV TTL 24h + KMS encryption is acceptable for pilot. We’ll run an internal privacy review before full rollout.

Please send the final commitment worksheet (line-item pricing for committed GPUs, burst credits, and launch-protection windows) and a simple runbook for canary + pre-warm steps. We aim to run the pilot canary next Tuesday (2026-11-10 09:00 PT), so we need the pre-warm checklist and the contact list for on-call ops engineers.

-Sanjay
